content:
Comparator Live (https://comparator.live.lean-lang.org/) currently fails on the "Latest Mathlib with Lean..." toolchain before any validation takes place. Every submission fails at the "Building Challenge" step with:

Building Challenge
info: mathlib: URL has changed; deleting '/project/.lake/packages/mathlib' and cloning again
error: read-only file system (error code: 4294967266)
  file: /project/.lake/packages/mathlib/docs/1000.yaml
uncaught exception: Child exited with 1

It looks like lake detects a changed Mathlib URL (Reservoir resolution vs. direct git URL?) and tries to delete and re-clone the package inside the sandbox overlay, where /project/.lake/packages is read-only by design — so the build dies before the challenge is even compiled.

This is reproducible with any challenge/solution pair on that toolchain, including ones previously validated and trusted in the browser. My own file has no Mathlib dependency at all (pure core Lean 4), so presumably rebuilding the server-side project would fix it.

Happy to provide more details if useful. Thanks for this tool — it's been very valuable for making certified proofs re-checkable in the browser with nothing to install.

Today the bug that I mentioned yesterday is fixed. The link to the Experimental Comparator Live at https://vidal-rosset.net/2026-05-01-core-logic-is-not-paraconsistent.html#org033d39a validates the proof again.

@Joseph Tooby-Smith thanks for sending the report — I noticed it was down about an hour later (because of a different zulip dm, but would have noticed this shortly thereafter), and will get some better reporting in place for comparator failures like this in the future.

FWIW: that error message came from lake and was somewhat misleading (see lean4#12901, lean4#13101) — the problem was I believe that a glibc update temporarily broke comparator's ability to call git, and that's the message you get when that happens.
Woah sorry, I meant @Joseph Vidal-Rosset
